hints.content:
The graph of $y=3^x$ can be transformed
to get the graph of $y=3^{x+2}+3$. 
[[☃ explanation 1]]

Note it is important to follow order of operations when building the function, as function transformations are not always commutative.  [[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation:
Suppose $f(x)=3^x$ and $g(x)=3^{x+2}+3$.  

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=3^x\\\\
f(x+2)&=3^{x+2}\\\\
f(x+2)+3&=3^{x+2}+3\\\\
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=f(x+2)+3$.  

Since function $g$ can be built from function $f$, the graph of function $g$ is a transformation of the graph of function $f$.

Consider the graph of $y=2^x$.

If we shift the graph of $y=2^x$ down $2$ units, and then reflect this across the $x$-axis, we get the following graph.

![An exponential function graph on an x y coordinate plane. Both x and y axes scale by two. The graph decreases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (zero, one) and (two, negative two). Its asymptote is at y equals two.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/b933a4b1e376db6a8d45454cf7b59625c351c5ec)

However, if we first reflect the graph of $y=2^x$ across the $x$-axis and then shift this graph down $2$ units, we get the following graph.

![An exponential function graph on an x y coordinate plane. Both x and y axes scale by two. The graph decreases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (zero, negative three) and (two, negative six). Its asymptote is at y equals negative two.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6532a044950cf696d6fbc8a2ef2c2c89f37c8635)

These graphs are not the same, indicating that the order in which you perform the transformations is important!

hints.content:
Replacing $x$ with $x+2$ shifts the graph of $y=3^x$ to the left $2$ units.  


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: An exponential function graph and its shifted graph on an x y coordinate plane. Both x and y axes scale by two. The graph increases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (zero, one) and (one, three). Its asymptote is at y equals zero. The shifted graph increases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (negative two, one) and (zero, nine). Its asymptote is at y equals zero.

hints.content:
Adding $3$ to the function shifts the graph of $y=3^{x+2}$ up $3$ units.

[[☃ image 1]]

Since the graph of $y=3^{x+2}$ had a horizontal asymptote of $y=0$, the graph of $y=3^{x+2}+3$ has a horizontal asymptote of $y=3$.

options.alt: An exponential function graph and its shifted graph on an x y coordinate plane. Both x and y axes scale by two. The graph increases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (negative two, one) and (zero, nine). Its asymptote is at y equals zero. The shifted graph increases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (negative two, four) and (zero, twelve). Its asymptote is at y equals three.

An exponential function graph on an x y coordinate plane. Both x and y axes scale by two. The graph increases from the interval negative infinity to infinity. It passes through (negative two, four) and (negative one, six). Its asymptote is at y equals three.
